parsed.reason: The page was genuinely read (page_has_schedule) and it explicitly states "Our youngest program starts at age 8. We do not offer preschool or toddler classes." Empty slots is therefore the correct and honest result — there is nothing for a toddler. The message, however, fails on multiple counts: (1) It hedges ("I could not confirm which, if any, apply to toddlers") instead of plainly reporting what the page actually says — that there are no toddler classes at all. The page gave a clear negative finding; Hale is licensed and required to report it plainly and specifically. (2) The watch=true flag means Hale has already written a continuation-watch promise, so "I'll keep watching and text you when I can tie a class to that age" is appropriate in form — but the premise it rests on ("when I can tie a class to that age") implies a class might exist to be tied, which misrepresents the page's explicit statement that no toddler program exists. The continuation sentence is not wrong merely because watch=true, but its framing subtly contradicts the honest finding. (3) The message says "I could not confirm" framing, which per the scoring rules is a first-person failure claim appropriate when page_has_schedule and Hale couldn't extract facts — but here the page *explicitly* says there are no toddler classes, so this is not a case of Hale failing to extract; it is a genuine negative result. The message should say plainly "their site says they don't offer toddler or preschool classes; their youngest program starts at age 8" rather than hedging as if the information might exist but was unconfirmed. The slots are correctly empty, but the message misrepresents a clear, page-supported negative finding as personal uncertainty, which is a meaningful flaw.
